title: Flow Tabs Build Plan
eyebrow: Build plan for approval · issues #248 to #259
approval: Build plan approved: tabs that follow the flow

short.lead: This builds the three designs you approved: the combined plan, part 2 and part 3. The work is one parent issue (#248) and eleven steps, in the order you chose: priority and Review first, then Tidy up, Triage and the Roadmap, with the new tabs last. The Board and Projects screens stay until the Roadmap can do everything they do, so nothing goes missing part way through. I test each step myself before starting the next: the automatic tests, plus a check in a real browser at phone and computer widths. You test once, at the end, from one QA page (a page of checks for you to try) that numbers the tests for each of the eleven steps.
short.hint: Tap a step to see what it builds and the design picture it follows.
items: Pick a priority on every add, and set a due date in one tap

Every way of adding a task needs a priority, except the jotter: a jotted thought gets its priority in Sort. Due date has one-tap buttons and starts on None. On a task card, the priority and due date become chips you tap to change.

items.alt: Phone: adding a task with priority and due date buttons
items.caption: Step 1, as approved in part 2.

items: Add Review as a fourth task status
Tasks can be Up next, In progress, Review or Done. GitHub's "needs review" label follows a task into and out of Review, and tasks you add in the app can be in Review too.

items.alt: A milestone with Up next, In progress, Review and Done columns
items.caption: The fourth column, as approved in part 3.

items: Areas and kinds of work in Settings
Project categories become Areas, starting with your eight areas. Your existing categories carry over. Settings also gets the tick list of which labels are kinds of work and which count as a priority.

items.alt: Settings showing the Areas list on desktop and phone
items.caption: Step 3, as approved.

items: The All / Area / Project switch on every screen
The same switch sits at the top of every screen and keeps your choice as you move between them. It replaces the Board's own filters.

items.alt: The All, Area and Project switch at the top of several screens
items.caption: Step 4, as approved in part 2.

items: One carousel for Focus and Sort

Desktop Focus gets the phone's carousels, five cards at a time, with arrow keys and the mouse. Sort picks a thought's project from the same carousel. 'Or let me pick for you' replaces the separate Start here screen.

items.alt: Focus with the project and kind-of-work carousels on desktop and phone
items.caption: Step 5, as approved in part 3.

items: 'Waiting for your review' has 'Looks good · Done' and 'Needs more work' on each task. 'Done this week' lists what you finished, with Undo.
Tidy up groups what looks finished, repeated or forgotten, and says why each task is there. Nothing closes until you press Confirm, and a closed task can be undone.

items.alt: Tidy up on desktop and phone
items.caption: Step 7, as approved.

items: Triage ranks what is left into Now, Next and Later by seven rules, with Review first. Your dragged order wins over the rules.

The Roadmap shows a group of projects or one project, with sections, milestones and four columns per milestone. You can drag tasks, milestones and sections. New project, Edit project and Sync now move here from the Projects screen.

items.alt: Roadmap for the Apps area on desktop and phone
items.caption: Step 9, as approved.

items: Each milestone gets a slider for how much it counts toward the project's percent, starting from equal shares, and one of four ways to measure it. The project's percent adds up its milestones by those shares.

items.alt: Milestone settings on desktop and phone
items.caption: Step 10, as approved.

items: Five tabs and the jot box on every tab

The menu becomes Sort, Organize (Tidy up and Triage), Roadmap, Focus and Review, with the jot box on every tab and the J key on desktop. The Board and Projects screens are removed last, once every feature they had works from its new home.

items.alt: The five tabs with the jot box above them
items.caption: Step 11, as approved in part 3.

items: The build starts with step 1 when you send your approval. I check each step before moving on. When all eleven are done, you get one QA page that numbers the tests for each step and its new features.
Reply "Build plan approved: tabs that follow the flow", or say what to change.
